# Prolongations of Simple Lie Algebras and Lie Superalgebras with Cartan Matrix

## Overview of the Study

This study investigates the prolongations of simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras and Lie superalgebras that possess a Cartan matrix, working over algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p > 2$. The theory of Lie algebras and superalgebras in positive characteristic exhibits rich structural phenomena that distinguish it from the classical case over fields of characteristic zero, making it a fertile area for the discovery of new algebraic objects.

## Focus of the Analysis

The central approach of this research is to examine certain of the simplest gradings of these algebras and superalgebras. By concentrating on these fundamental gradings, we are able to systematically construct and study the prolongations that arise, thereby uncovering the underlying structural properties of the algebras in question. This methodology provides a tractable framework for identifying new examples and understanding their behavior.

## Discovery of New Simple Lie Superalgebras

One of the principal outcomes of this investigation is the discovery of several new simple Lie superalgebras. These newly found superalgebras encompass both serial families—that is, infinite series parametrized by dimension or rank—and exceptional cases that stand apart from any regular series. The existence of such objects highlights the considerable diversity of simple Lie superalgebras that emerge specifically in the setting of positive characteristic.

## The SuperBrown and SuperMelikyan Superalgebras

Among the newly identified superalgebras are two notable examples: the superBrown and the superMelikyan superalgebras. These are super-analogues of previously known Lie algebras, extending the classical Brown and Melikyan constructions to the super setting. Their discovery enriches the known catalogue of exceptional simple Lie superalgebras and demonstrates how established characteristic-$p$ phenomena can find natural counterparts in super-mathematics.

## Complete Classification in Rank 2

Finally, this study achieves a complete classification of the simple Lie superalgebras with Cartan matrix of rank 2. This classification represents a significant and concrete result, providing an exhaustive description of all such superalgebras in the rank-2 case. It serves both as a foundational reference for further work and as a demonstration of the effectiveness of the prolongation and grading techniques employed throughout the research.

# Prolongations and Classification of Simple Lie Superalgebras with Cartan Matrix in Positive Characteristic

## Introduction and Setting

This work is carried out over algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p > 2$. In this setting, the theory of simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras and Lie superalgebras diverges dramatically from the classical picture familiar over fields of characteristic zero. Whereas the complex or real theory is governed by a clean and complete classification, positive characteristic introduces a wealth of additional structures that have no characteristic-zero analogues. Understanding these structures—and, ultimately, classifying them—remains one of the central problems in modular representation theory and modular Lie theory.

The principal objects of study here are simple Lie algebras and Lie superalgebras that possess a Cartan matrix. Such algebras generalize the classical construction in which a Cartan matrix encodes the relations among Chevalley generators. In the modular setting, however, a given Cartan matrix may give rise to algebras with subtle and unexpected features, and the passage to superalgebras—where a $\mathbb{Z}/2$-grading distinguishes even and odd elements—further enriches the possibilities.

## Prolongations and Gradings

A central technical tool in this investigation is the notion of a *prolongation*. Given a Lie algebra or superalgebra equipped with a grading, one may attempt to reconstruct or extend it by building up its graded components step by step, starting from the non-positive part and generating the positive components through a universal procedure known as the Cartan prolongation. This method, going back to Cartan's work on infinite-dimensional Lie pseudogroups and later formalized in the study of $\mathbb{Z}$-graded Lie algebras, is especially powerful for producing and recognizing exceptional structures.

We focus on prolongations associated with certain of the *simplest gradings*—those short gradings, typically of depth one, that are most amenable to explicit computation and that nevertheless capture the essential structural information. By systematically analyzing the prolongations of simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras and Lie superalgebras with Cartan matrix for these gradings, one obtains both a means of verifying known examples and, crucially, a mechanism for uncovering new ones.

## Classification in Rank 2

A concrete and complete result of this study is the classification of all rank-2 simple Lie superalgebras with Cartan matrix. Rank 2 is the first genuinely nontrivial case: rank 1 is too rigid to exhibit interesting phenomena, while rank 2 already displays the full complexity of the interplay between the Cartan matrix, the characteristic of the field, and the super-structure. Carrying out this classification requires a careful case-by-case analysis of the admissible Cartan matrices, the resulting defining relations, and the conditions under which the associated algebra is simple. The outcome provides a definitive list for this rank and serves as a foundation for higher-rank investigations.

## New Simple Lie Superalgebras

The most striking outcome of the investigation is the discovery of several previously unknown simple Lie superalgebras. These fall into two categories:

- **Serial superalgebras**, which occur in infinite families parametrized by rank or dimension, extending recognizable patterns across the modular landscape.
- **Exceptional superalgebras**, which appear only for specific small parameters and specific characteristics, and which therefore represent genuinely sporadic phenomena.

Among the exceptional examples are the **superBrown** and **superMelikyan** superalgebras. These are super-analogues of the well-known Brown algebras and Melikyan algebras—themselves exceptional simple Lie algebras that exist only in small positive characteristics (the Melikyan algebras, for instance, live in characteristic $5$). The construction of their super counterparts demonstrates that the exceptional phenomena of modular Lie theory persist, and indeed proliferate, when one passes to the super setting.

## Significance

Taken together, these results substantially expand the known landscape of simple Lie algebras and superalgebras with Cartan matrix in positive characteristic. By combining the prolongation technique with a complete rank-2 classification, the work not only organizes existing knowledge but also demonstrates that the modular super-world contains more structures than had been previously catalogued. The newly discovered serial and exceptional superalgebras—particularly the superBrown and superMelikyan examples—enlarge the inventory of objects that any eventual complete classification must accommodate, and they underscore the richness and continuing surprises of Lie theory over fields of positive characteristic.

# Lie Algebras and the Cartan Framework

## Introduction

The study of continuous symmetry has become one of the central themes of modern mathematics, and much of its language traces back to the work of **Sophus Lie** and **Élie Cartan**. Together, their contributions form the backbone of what we now call the theory of Lie groups and Lie algebras, structures that appear naturally across geometry, physics, and abstract algebra.

## Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

A **Lie group** is a smooth manifold equipped with a group structure in which multiplication and inversion are smooth operations. To each Lie group there corresponds a **Lie algebra**, which captures the group's local behavior near the identity element. The Lie algebra is a vector space endowed with a bilinear, antisymmetric operation called the *bracket*, satisfying the Jacobi identity.

This linearization is remarkably powerful: many questions about a curved, nonlinear group can be translated into linear-algebraic problems posed **over** a field—typically the real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ or the complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. The choice of the base field profoundly affects the classification and the available techniques.

## Cartan's Contributions

Élie Cartan brought extraordinary depth to this subject. Among his lasting achievements are:

- **Cartan subalgebras**, maximal abelian subalgebras that act diagonally and provide the essential coordinate system for understanding a Lie algebra's structure.
- The **Cartan criterion**, which distinguishes semisimple Lie algebras through the nondegeneracy of the *Killing form*.
- The classification of **simple Lie algebras** over the complex numbers, organized elegantly through root systems and Dynkin diagrams.

By decomposing a Lie algebra relative to the action of a Cartan subalgebra, one obtains a system of **roots**—vectors that encode the entire algebraic architecture. This decomposition works cleanly over an algebraically closed field, revealing symmetries that might otherwise remain hidden.

## The Role of the Base Field

Working **over** different fields introduces subtle richness. Over $\mathbb{C}$, the classification is complete and clean. Over $\mathbb{R}$, one must account for various *real forms* of the same complex algebra, a problem that Cartan himself resolved through his analysis of symmetric spaces. Over more general fields, questions of rationality and Galois cohomology come into play, extending the theory into arithmetic domains.

## Conclusion

The interplay of **Lie**'s structural insight, **Cartan**'s classifying genius, and the flexibility of constructions **over** varying fields continues to shape mathematics today. From particle physics to differential geometry, this framework provides a unifying language for describing symmetry in all its forms.

## Abstract

We study the Tanaka–Weisfeiler prolongations of non-positively graded simple Lie algebras and Lie superalgebras with indecomposable Cartan matrices over algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p > 2$. In the modular and super settings, the interplay between the root system, the Cartan matrix, and the grading gives rise to phenomena that have no analogue in characteristic zero: partial or infinite prolongations, exceptional isomorphisms in small characteristics, and the appearance of new simple structures not obtained by reduction modulo $p$ of characteristic-zero Lie (super)algebras.

Starting from a $\mathbb{Z}$-grading $\mathfrak{g} = \bigoplus_{i \geq -d} \mathfrak{g}_i$ determined by a subset of simple roots, we compute the complete and partial prolongations of the non-positive part $\mathfrak{g}_{\leq 0}$, giving a uniform description of the resulting graded Lie (super)algebras in terms of generalized Cartan-type constructions. Particular attention is paid to the characteristics $p = 3$ and $p = 5$, where degenerations of the Cartan matrix produce additional simple algebras, and to the role of the Bouarroudj–Grozman–Leites classification of finite-dimensional modular Lie superalgebras with Cartan matrix. We determine which prolongations remain finite-dimensional, identify their simple subquotients, and describe the associated Weisfeiler filtrations.

Our results extend the classical prolongation techniques of Cartan, Tanaka, and Weisfeiler to the modular and super framework, clarify the structure of the exceptional families arising in low characteristic, and provide explicit generators and defining relations for the algebras obtained. As applications, we discuss consequences for the classification of simple $\mathbb{Z}$-graded Lie (super)algebras of finite depth and for the construction of new non-restricted simple Lie superalgebras in characteristic $p > 2$.

---

*Keywords:* modular Lie algebras, Lie superalgebras, Cartan matrix, Tanaka–Weisfeiler prolongation, positive characteristic, Cartan-type algebras, $\mathbb{Z}$-gradings.

# Abstract

We present a complete classification of finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebras admitting a Cartan matrix over algebraically closed fields of positive characteristic, focusing on those of rank 2. Building upon the framework of Cartan matrices and their associated Chevalley-type generators, we analyze the constraints imposed by the rank-2 condition and systematically enumerate the resulting superalgebras, including their inequivalent Cartan matrices related by odd and even reflections.

Our investigation reveals the existence of two previously unknown families of simple modular Lie superalgebras, which we designate the **superBrown** and **superMelikyan** superalgebras. These arise as super-analogues of the classical Brown and Melikyan Lie algebras known in the modular (finite characteristic) setting, and they emerge specifically in small characteristics where exceptional phenomena are known to occur. For each superalgebra in the classification, we provide the explicit Cartan matrix, the associated Dynkin-type diagram, dimension formulas, and the structure of the even and odd parts. The superBrown and superMelikyan superalgebras exhibit distinctive features absent in characteristic zero, underscoring the richness of the modular super setting and the necessity of computer-aided verification in confirming defining relations. These results contribute to the broader program of classifying simple Lie superalgebras in positive characteristic and highlight the exceptional structures that populate the small-characteristic landscape.

# Prolongations and Simple Gradings of Modular Lie Superalgebras

Research on modular Lie superalgebras (over fields of characteristic *p* > 0) has focused heavily on **Cartan prolongations** as a tool for constructing and classifying simple examples, generalizing the classical characteristic-0 theory of Cartan-type Lie (super)algebras. The core idea, going back to work formalized by **Shchepochkina** (via her algorithm for computing prolongs, including the more subtle *complete* and *partial* prolongations), is to start from a **nonpositive part** $\mathfrak{g}_{-} \oplus \mathfrak{g}_0$ — typically a negatively graded nilpotent piece together with a subalgebra $\mathfrak{g}_0 \subset \mathfrak{der}(\mathfrak{g}_{-})$ acting on it — and generate the positive part by prolongation, yielding a $\mathbb{Z}$-graded Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{g} = \bigoplus_i \mathfrak{g}_i$.

In characteristic *p* several phenomena appear that have no characteristic-0 analog:

- **New simple algebras and "deforms"** arise, and prolongations can be infinite where they would be finite classically (or vice versa), so the depth and consistency of the grading become delicate.
- **Divided-power structures** replace the polynomial coordinates, giving the Lie superalgebras of vector fields their modular flavor (e.g., $\mathfrak{vect}$, $\mathfrak{svect}$, contact and periplectic-contact series).
- Small primes (**p = 2, 3, 5**) are exceptional; in particular **p = 2** requires a careful redefinition of "Lie superalgebra" (via quadratic forms / squaring maps), and this is where much recent work by **Bouarroudj, Grozman, Lebedev, Leites** and collaborators has uncovered many sporadic simple examples.

The classification program — determining which $(\mathfrak{g}_{-}, \mathfrak{g}_0)$ pairs yield simple prolongs, and organizing the resulting "simplest" ($\mathbb{Z}$- or $\mathbb{Z}/n$-) gradings — remains open in general, but large families and exceptional cases in low ranks and small characteristics have been catalogued, often with substantial computer assistance (SuperLie and related packages).

---

# Abstract

The classification of finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebras over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero, while achieved by Kac, admits a natural and productive extension through the framework of Cartan prolongations. In this work, we investigate the Cartan prolongation of the non-positive part of $\mathbb{Z}$-graded Lie superalgebras and demonstrate how this construction yields both infinite-dimensional linearly compact simple Lie superalgebras and, under suitable finiteness and irreducibility conditions on the underlying $\mathfrak{g}_0$-module $\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$, novel finite-dimensional simple superalgebras. We provide a systematic analysis of the prolongation data $(\mathfrak{g}_{-1}, \mathfrak{g}_0)$, classifying those pairs for which the full prolongation $\mathfrak{g} = \bigoplus_{k \geq -1} \mathfrak{g}_k$ terminates in finite depth and gives rise to simple structures. Our approach unifies the treatment of the classical series with the exceptional cases, clarifying the role of transitivity and the bracket-induced pairing $\mathfrak{g}_{-1} \otimes \mathfrak{g}_1 \to \mathfrak{g}_0$ in controlling prolongation length.

As a central result, we identify several new serial families of simple superalgebras arising as prolongations of vectorial type, together with a finite list of exceptional superalgebras not previously catalogued, whose existence depends on sporadic isomorphisms among low-rank orthosymplectic and periplectic modules. For each newly found algebra we compute the associated $\mathbb{Z}$-grading, describe the consistent even/odd decomposition, and verify simplicity via an analysis of graded ideals. We further establish structural properties including the derivation superalgebra, the invariant bilinear forms (when they exist), and the compatibility of the prolongation with the induced filtration. These results extend the Weisfeiler–Kac program to the super setting and suggest connections to the geometry of $G$-structures on supermanifolds, where the exceptional prolongations correspond to superanalogues of exceptional simple transitive geometries.

---

*Keywords:* Lie superalgebras, Cartan prolongation, simple superalgebras, $\mathbb{Z}$-gradings, exceptional superalgebras, orthosymplectic and periplectic modules.
